Northeast Georgia Health System (NGHS) seeks an accomplished healthcare compliance executive to serve as its next Chief Compliance Officer. This is a significant opportunity to guide enterprise compliance strategy, influence executive decision-making, and strengthen the trust at the heart of our mission: improving the health of our communities. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving on the NGHS senior leadership team, the Chief Compliance Officer will lead ethics, privacy, and internal audit compliance efforts. This leader will bring strategic vision, independent judgment, and a collaborative approach to helping NGHS navigate complex requirements while supporting its organizational and clinical priorities. An Opportunity to Make a Lasting Impact The Chief Compliance Officer will partner with executive leaders, physicians, Legal, Human Resources, and operational teams to build a proactive, effective compliance program. Success will require a leader who can anticipate risk, translate complex requirements into practical guidance, and inspire accountability throughout the organization. Advance enterprise compliance strategy: Lead a comprehensive program addressing applicable federal and state healthcare requirements, including HIPAA, Stark Law, and the Anti-Kickback Statute. Strengthen oversight and accountability: Provide meaningful reporting and guidance to the Compliance Oversight Committee, executive leadership, and Board of Trustees. Identify and address risk: Direct risk assessments, coding and billing audits, monitoring, investigations, and corrective action plans. Champion ethics and privacy: Promote the Code of Conduct, strengthen privacy practices, and oversee the Compliance Hotline and other reporting mechanisms. Lead critical compliance commitments: Oversee implementation and administration of the Corporate Integrity Agreement in partnership with the CEO. Build organizational capability: Develop education for employees, executives, and board members that makes compliance an integral part of daily decisions. The ideal candidate combines deep healthcare compliance expertise with the ability to build relationships, develop teams, and balance organizational growth with compliance responsibilities. We’re a growth-stage software company helping manufacturers access, structure, and use real-time data from machines, systems, and sensors at the edge. Our platform sits at the intersection of edge computing, AI, and industrial operations, enabling some of the world’s largest companies to run operations in real time, reduce downtime, and optimize production. Backed by leading investors and trusted by global manufacturers and partners like Google, Microsoft, Dell, Oracle, and Mitsubishi, Litmus is powering the shift toward software-defined manufacturing. Why join Litmus Build the infrastructure that makes industrial AI possible AI is moving beyond the cloud and into the physical world. At Litmus, you’ll build the infrastructure that enables real-time data to power AI and machine learning systems in production environments. Work on problems where software meets the real world Most AI systems fail without access to real-world data. You’ll build the layer that makes them viable in production. We solve challenges at the intersection of distributed systems, real-time data, and industrial constraints — where reliability, scale, and performance are non-negotiable. Have real impact, fast You’ll work on systems used by real customers in production, with direct impact on product and company trajectory. As a scaling company, we move quickly. You’ll have ownership, visibility, and the ability to shape both product and company as we scale. Join a high-performance team We’re building a team that holds a high bar and pushes each other to improve. You’ll work alongside experienced operators, engineers, and leaders who have done this before and are building again at scale. We hire people who take ownership, move quickly, and care about outcomes. No passengers. Our culture At Litmus, the team is collaborative, curious, and low ego. People are scrappy, take ownership, and look for ways to make an impact. We value empathy just as much as execution, whether that’s in how we build, how we communicate, or how we support each other. We’re a growing company, so things move quickly and not everything is perfectly defined. If you enjoy figuring things out, working closely with others, and making steady progress, you’ll do well here. About The Role Litmus is hiring an Account Executive to own and grow new business with industrial manufacturers across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland and Finland. Litmus is an industrial DataOps and edge AI platform. We help manufacturers connect, normalize and use data from their plants, from shop-floor assets up to the cloud. Our customers use Litmus to break down OT data silos and scale analytics and AI across sites. You will be the face of Litmus in the Nordics. You will build pipeline, run complex enterprise sales cycles end to end, and work closely with our pre-sales team, hyperscaler partners (Microsoft, AWS, Google, Databricks) and system integrators. You report to the EMEA sales lead. What You Will Do Own a Nordic territory and its revenue target, from prospecting to signed contract and expansion. Build and qualify pipeline through outbound, events, partners and inbound leads. Run discovery with plant, operations, OT and IT stakeholders up to C-level, and map their business case for change. Lead structured, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles, including proofs of value, commercial proposals and negotiation. Work hand in hand with pre-sales on demos, solution design and technical validation. Co-sell with hyperscalers and system integrators, and develop partner-sourced opportunities in your region. Keep forecasts and opportunity data accurate in Salesforce. Expand existing accounts from first site to multi-site and global rollouts. Bring market feedback back to product, marketing and leadership. What You Bring Segment experience (required) 5+ years of B2B enterprise software sales, with a proven record of meeting or beating quota. Direct sales experience in industrial software: IIoT, industrial DataOps, data historians, MES, SCADA, edge computing or manufacturing analytics. A solid grasp of the OT/IT landscape in manufacturing, and of how plant data flows from machines to the cloud. Experience selling into manufacturing, process industries, energy or similar industrial sectors. Nordic Market Knowledge (required) An established network among industrial manufacturers in the Nordics. A working understanding of Nordic buying culture, decision-making and procurement. Familiarity with the regional partner and system integrator landscape. Fluency in English and at least one Nordic language (Swedish, Norwegian, Danish or Finnish). How You Work Comfortable running long, complex deals with many stakeholders. Disciplined in qualification and forecasting (MEDDIC/MEDDPICC or similar). Self-driven and at ease building a territory in a growing team. Nice to have Experience selling alongside Microsoft, AWS, Google or Databricks. Track record of displacing incumbent industrial software, such as historians or legacy integration tools. Experience in an early-stage or scale-up team in a new region. Travel and location Up to 40% travel within the Nordics and to EMEA team and partner events. Based in the Nordics, ideally near Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen or Helsinki.
